scientific_hypothesis: The global minimum for mean reflectance in this constrained two-layer system occurs with the SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the TiO2 layer adjacent to glass, with thicknesses perturbed slightly from the ideal quarter-wave values (SiO2 ~99nm, TiO2 ~60nm) to balance the broadband response. The reverse order (TiO2/SiO2) cannot achieve a lower mean reflectance even with optimal thickness tuning due to the impedance mismatch profile at the air interface.
expected_advantages: Initialization near the physical optimum reduces the risk of the optimizer converging to a shallow local minimum far from the quarter-wave solution.
Explicitly testing the reverse order with equal optimization effort provides a definitive comparison rather than relying on potentially under-optimized baseline results from Round 1.
known_risks: The optimal solution might lie at the boundary of the thickness constraints (40 or 160 nm) if the quarter-wave condition is incompatible with the broadband requirement.
The discrete nature of the stack order means the optimizer must evaluate both topologies; if the search budget is split too thinly, one order might be under-explored.
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase as the optimizer identifies the superior stack order and converges on optimal thicknesses.
valid_candidates should remain high unless the thickness constraints force all candidates to invalid states (unlikely given the wide range).
tightest_margin should stabilize as the solution approaches the thickness boundaries or a local minimum.
If neither order achieves the soft target, best_target_score will plateau below the threshold corresponding to 0.03 reflectance.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best.
If valid_candidates drops to zero due to constraint violations (unexpected), stop and report the constraint conflict.
